title: A split maximal torus is its own scheme-theoretic centralizer
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring and let $G$ be a split reductive $A$-group scheme with split maximal torus $T=D_A(M)$, in the sense of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization] after forgetting the pinning. The centralizer functor $C_G(T)$, whose $B$-points are elements of $G(B)$ commuting with every element of $T(B')$ after every commutative $B$-algebra extension $B'$, is represented by the closed subgroup $T\subseteq G$. This equality is scheme-theoretic and remains valid after arbitrary base change $A\to B$, including nonreduced and disconnected base rings.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4 and Corollary 3.3.6(1), printed pp.98--101; self-centrality of a maximal torus and its arbitrary-base change formulation. Read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Choose a basis of the finite-rank free lattice $M$ in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization], of rank $r\geq0$. The basis elements in [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group] give $A[M]\simeq A[z_1,w_1,\ldots,z_r,w_r]/(z_iw_i-1)_{i=1}^r$, so $T$ is affine and finitely presented by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Its points are tuples of units and commute, since the coproduct $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$ is symmetric. To check formal smoothness, for a square-zero ideal $I\subset R$ lift each unit and its inverse from $R/I$ to $u,v\in R$. Write $uv=1+e$, $e\in I$; then $u\,v(1-e)=1$ since $e^2=0$. Thus all unit tuples lift, including the unique empty tuple when $r=0$. By [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is smooth.

The reductive group $G$ is smooth affine of finite presentation, and $T$ is a closed split torus. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer], using the coordinates of step 1. It represents the full centralizer by a smooth affine finitely presented closed subgroup $C\subseteq G$ and identifies its arbitrary base changes with the corresponding centralizers. Since $T$ is commutative, its inclusion factors through $C$. The resulting $i:T\to C$ is a closed immersion: if $G=\operatorname{Spec}H$, $C=\operatorname{Spec}(H/J_C)$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}(H/J_T)$, the factorization says $J_C\subseteq J_T$, and $i$ corresponds to the surjection $H/J_C\to H/J_T$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.4, printed pp.64--66; centralizer functor of Definition 2.2.1

proof.text: Check the finite-presentation hypothesis for $i$, rather than assuming that every closed immersion has it. Write $C=\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], $E$ is a finitely presented $A$-algebra; choose a surjection $A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to E$. The composite surjection to the finitely presented algebra $F=A[M]$ has finitely generated kernel by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-surjection-kernel-fg]. Its image is the kernel of $E\to F$, so that kernel is generated by the images of the same finite list. Thus $F=E/(h_1,\ldots,h_q)$ is finitely presented over $E$, and $i$ is locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

For each geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, the defining hypotheses make $G_\Omega$ reductive and $T_\Omega$ a maximal torus. Step 2 identifies $C_\Omega$ with the full centralizer of $T_\Omega$ in $G_\Omega$. Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer] over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$. It identifies that centralizer with $T_\Omega$ as a subgroup functor on all $\Omega$-algebras. Hence the actual inclusion $i_\Omega:T_\Omega\to C_\Omega$ is an isomorphism, including its scheme structure.

By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], the smooth morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. The target $C$ is finitely presented over $A$, hence locally of finite type; step 3 supplies local finite presentation of $i$. With the geometric-fibre isomorphisms of step 4, all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-flat-geometric-fibre-open-criterion] hold for $X=T$, $Y=C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its isomorphism clause proves that $i$ is an isomorphism. Since its composite with $C\hookrightarrow G$ is the specified torus inclusion, this proves $C_G(T)=T$ as closed subgroup schemes of $G$.

source.place: Tag 039E (lemma-morphism-between-flat), via the cited geometric-fibre isomorphism criterion

proof.text: Let $A\to B$ be any ring map. The base-change clause of [lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer] identifies the full centralizer of $T_B$ in $G_B$ with $C_B$. Base-changing $i$ and its inverse gives inverse maps $T_B\rightleftarrows C_B$ whose composites with $G_B$ are the inclusions. Therefore $C_{G_B}(T_B)=T_B$ scheme-theoretically. This uses no reducedness, connectedness, flatness or nonzeroness of $B$; for $B=0$ both schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}B=\varnothing$ are empty. Nonreduced and disconnected test algebras are already part of the full centralizer functor, so the conclusion includes them.
